pr_body:
This commit adds functionality to fork a repository into an organization.

Closes #1247
pr_comments: @mislav I'd like some insight on how I can simulate a 403 response when the user doesn't have WRITE permission on the organization. I'm stuck at that last test case. Would be helpful if you gave some advice. Thank you :)

issue_context.title: gh repo fork cannot fork to org
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I want to fork a repo from the cli, but not to my personal account.

### Proposed solution

Maybe a flag like `--org` or `--to`?
comments:
I don't see a reason why we shouldn't do this! I think it was originally left out due to an oversight.

@mislav do you know off the top of the head if this would require re-authenticating for increased privileges for orgs?

> do you know off the top of the head if this would require re-authenticating for increased privileges for orgs?

I don't know, since I only have experience of forking a repo to an org using the REST API. Since GraphQL sometimes requires extra scopes, in this case `write:org` may be required, but we could try it out and check. 👍
bluh, other issue's author was deleted so i'm making this one canonical
Any progress on the "gh repo fork --to-org" ?
@vilmibm I have a working PR which implements `--to-org`. Would you like to have a look at it?
@g14a You are welcome to submit your PR!

@mislav do you have a set of features that `--to-org` must implement? This is an old PR(since its been two months) and I need to add tests as well. Right now just `gh repo fork user/repo --to-org batmanshome` works, where `batmanshome` is the organization to which I have write access to. Do you have anymore validations in your mind or edge cases where it should or shouldn't work?

@g14a Let's keep the feature simple and call the flag just `--org MYORG`.

Ideally I would love to see functionality like `gh repo fork user/repo --to myorg/another-name`, so you can edit the name of the new repository as well, but this is not possible via API right now, so let's just take the org name as input.

review_comments: Same here: consider letting the test case define its own expected output.
Let's use JSON encoding functionality instead of writing it by hand.
Instead of switching stubs based on a boolean in the test case, consider letting the test case define its own stub.

I appreciate you adding this special case, but I think it might be premature optimization. The 401 error will be reported to the terminal via our usual error handling and I don't think we need to add anything on top of that. If the user doesn't have write access to their org, the fork command will fail with a visible 401 and it will be enough information for them to go on.

I appreciate you adding many extra tests, but all of these extra tests are completely unnecessary. The feature you've added is just unconditionally passing one extra parameter to the fork function. A single tests above is enough to exercise this functionality.
